messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: parameter labeling spec
parts:
On Wednesday, December 16, 2015 at 2:00:47 PM UTC-5, Alp Kucukelbir wrote:
please do share your thoughts and comment!

At the risk of fracturing the discussion into different places on the internet, is parameter tagging the best way to indicate distinctions among ADVI approaches? For example, block diagonal ADVI could be accomplished if there were an option for a user to pass in a proto covariance matrix where elements that were zero are constrained to be zero and elements that were non-zero are free (subject to the positive definiteness restriction). Or ADVI could support a second .stan file that specified how the multivariate normal distribution is parameterized / penalized.

Parameter tagging may be inevitable for MML, in which case having a general framework for it that might also allow ADVI to use it would be nice to have. But given that we haven't ever been close to achieving a consensus on that, I wouldn't want research on ADVI to get stuck waiting for that to happen.

Ben

into something here.

elaborate more? what do you have in mind?

considered this as a way of implementing BBVI (different from ADVI)

separate "pathway" as needed.

what say you?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] parameter labeling spec
parts:
I'd hold off on C++ specs.

What I mean by "outside" is outside of the modeling language. In
particular, you can have a call to CmdStan like:

./foo advi_bar phi="a, b, c, d"

where a, b, c, and d are the "phi" variables. This will make that
list of variables available to whatever solver you're using without
having to extract them from the model.

I'm not at all clear on why there'd be a separate Stan file.
It sounded like you only needed to evaluate the log prob function
and gradient the way it's being done now. What would a separate
Stan file be for?

I'm not sure what you mean by "slowly mold", but if it means
breaking backward compatibility as we go, I'm very strongly opposed.

- Bob

messages.author: 453ddfeccaf29bbb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] parameter labeling spec
parts:
@bob: that's a cool idea.

i think what ben was suggesting was simply a .stan file to hold all
those variable names that you suggest passing through the input.

i can imagine it being clunky to provide a long list of things via the
command line.

re slowly mold: there's nothing backward to break :) i'm just saying
that if we do something "outside of stan" (as you suggest), then it
would be easier to develop that since it doesn't touch the modeling
language. (as opposed to suggesting a change that touches the guts of
Stan.)

messages.author: 49e107cb0f8a3d27
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] parameter labeling spec
parts:
I also like Bob's idea. It removes the nastiness of putting algorithmic-specific labels into the Stan program, and allows you to change them at runtime. So for MML it would be

./foo mml hyperparameters=“phi" local="alpha"

and ADVI would be

./foo advi meanfield=“w” fullrank=“alpha, sigma”

Similar to external files for specifying inits, the labelling can be read in from an external file. This avoids writing long lists on the command line and not storing them each time. I also feel like we’re converging to this solution (at least in this thread), since the second “.stan” file is essentially trying to do this.

Dustin

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] parameter labeling spec
parts:
I would prefer that to putting something in the model, and
not just because it's a lot less work for me (though I'll admit
that is part of it).

Although I'm hesitant to suggest it, a common approach is
to add comments with specific forms. For instance, that's how
our doxygen documentation for the C++ API is generated. So
it'd be something like:

real alpha; // @fullrank
real<lower=0> sigma; // @fullrank

But I really really don't like the whole idea of meaningful
comments --- just throwing it out there. But if we do go
with variable annotations, it's going to have to be something
that scopes before the ; (just for syntactic sanity) and has
some marking, e.g.,

@fullrank
real alpha;

- Bob

On Thursday, December 17, 2015 at 1:42:09 PM UTC-5, Alp Kucukelbir wrote:
dustin and i are going to take the cmd line/init file approach and
develop a variant of ADVI that can leverage labeling. once we get this
working, we can revisit everything and decide whether we want to make
any modifications to the modeling language.

For block diagonal ADVI, I think this is the way to go. I was only suggesting the second Stan file as an alternative for more complicated versions of ADVI where, for example, one of the blocks is the sum of a low-rank matrix and a diagonal matrix or you have AR(1) structure or something.

Ben
